meta.topic: Build a RAG App with LangChain
meta.title: Build a RAG App with LangChain
meta.thesis: Build a RAG App with LangChain is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A LangChain docs assistant answers support questions but often cites the wrong page. By the end, they should be able to build or review RAG chain with retriever, prompt, citation contract, and faithfulness check, measure faithful answer rate on support questions, and catch the failure where the generated answer uses a plausible policy not present in retrieved chunks.

blocks.title: A LangChain app still needs a contract

spans.text: Problem anchor: a learner asks a LangChain-backed tutor why reranking improves RAG. The chain must answer from retrieved course notes, cite the note title, and refuse when the notes do not contain the answer.

LangChain gives many integrations, but the build should start with the behavior contract: what counts as evidence, how citations appear, what happens when retrieval is empty, and which questions prove the slice works.
Write the five acceptance questions before importing a vector store.

blocks.analogy: Build the smallest bridge you can load-test before opening the highway.

blocks.title: Worked contract: five questions and one refusal

spans.text: The LangChain prototype accepts a question, retrieves evidence from local Markdown notes, returns an answer with source titles, and logs retrieved chunks or nodes. It passes when four factual questions cite the expected source and the negative question refuses.

This artifact is small enough for a reviewer to inspect in one sitting, but complete enough to catch the failures that matter: missing evidence, noisy retrieval, unsupported claims, and silent fallback.

items.text: Pick three source files and record their source metadata.
Write five user-style questions with expected source titles.
Define answer, citation, and refusal requirements.
Run the slice before adding memory, chat history, or agents.

blocks.title: Document metadata is part of the answer

spans.text: A LangChain `Document` is more than `page_content`. Its metadata should carry source title, URL or path, heading, version, tenant, and category so retrieval can filter and the answer can cite.
Splitter settings should follow source structure first. Recursive splitting is useful, but a broken table or orphaned heading becomes a broken citation downstream.
Print sampled `Document` chunks before embedding and reject chunks whose metadata would not satisfy a reviewer.

blocks.analogy: The loader stamps the passport each chunk carries through the app.

blocks.title: Case study: from “Document 3” to useful source titles

spans.text: The first prototype returns citations like “Document 2,” which makes review painful. After ingestion stores human-readable titles and heading paths, the same answer becomes auditable.
No model changed; the app simply preserved provenance.

items.text: Split by source structure before token windows.
Attach title, URL/path, heading, and version metadata.
Print sample units and reject malformed ones.

modules.title: Retriever, prompt, and model are separate runnables
modules.sub: The core chain should expose each stage instead of hiding failures.
modules.summary: LangChain chains are easiest to debug when retrieval and generation remain separable.
objectives: Explain why retriever, prompt, and model are separate runnables matters for this LangChain build.
Prompt the model with explicit evidence boundaries.

blocks.title: Do not collapse the chain into one mystery call

spans.text: The retriever should be testable without the model. The prompt should show exactly which evidence chunks are passed. The model output should then be validated against those chunks.
LangChain runnable composition is useful because each stage can carry callbacks, traces, retries, and tests. Treat that observability as part of the design, not a later add-on.
A trace should show question, retrieved document IDs, prompt context, model answer, and citation validation result.

blocks.analogy: Do not debug the whole machine when one visible gear is slipping.

cells.text: Evidence present but answer misreads it.
UI cannot trust or render output.
Structured output, citation checks, refusal gate.

modules.title: Code the chain with evidence logging
modules.sub: A runnable slice should print retrieved Documents before answering.
modules.summary: The first useful LangChain implementation is boring, inspectable, and source-aware.
objectives: Explain why code the chain with evidence logging matters for this LangChain build.
Predict which source answers a test question.

blocks.title: The useful code path prints the evidence first

spans.text: A local toy retriever is acceptable for the first architecture check because it proves the control flow without external credentials. Once the trace contract works, swap in LangChain loaders, vector stores, and chat models.
Spaced recall: from RAG evaluation, judge the packed context that generation actually sees. Logging unused candidates does not prove the answer was grounded.
The code should make it obvious which source the answer cites.

blocks.title: LangChain-style RAG chain with trace
blocks.code:
from langchain_core.documents import Document

DOCS = [
    Document(page_content="Reranking reorders retrieved candidates before generation.", metadata={"source": "retrieval.md"}),
    Document(page_content="Chunking preserves answer evidence with headings and metadata.", metadata={"source": "chunking.md"}),
]

def retrieve(question):
    terms = set(question.lower().split())
    ranked = sorted(DOCS, key=lambda d: len(terms & set(d.page_content.lower().split())), reverse=True)
    return ranked[:2]

def answer(question):
    evidence = retrieve(question)
    print("TRACE", [(d.metadata["source"], d.page_content) for d in evidence])
    if not evidence or "reranking" not in evidence[0].page_content.lower():
        return "Not enough evidence."
    return f"Reranking reorders retrieved candidates before generation. Source: {evidence[0].metadata['source']}"

print(answer("What does reranking do before generation?"))
blocks.explanation: This uses a toy retriever so the control flow is runnable without external services; swap in LangChain loaders, vector stores, and models after the trace contract is clear.

predictThenReveal.prompt: Before running it, predict which source appears in TRACE for the reranking question.
predictThenReveal.answer: retrieval.md should appear first. If a real retriever disagrees, debug retrieval before changing answer style.

modules.title: Promote the chain into regression tests
modules.sub: LangChain changes should rerun source-based checks.
modules.summary: A LangChain RAG app is reviewable when failures are repeatable.
objectives: Explain why promote the chain into regression tests matters for this LangChain build.

blocks.title: The chain is not done until tests can fail it

spans.text: Record the expected source for each acceptance question and rerun the suite after changing loaders, splitters, retrievers, prompts, model versions, or LangChain packages.
The release bar should include packed-context hit rate, citation support, negative-case refusal, and trace completeness. A single happy-path chat transcript is not enough.
Every failed test should name a likely owner: ingestion, retrieval, prompt, validation, or source content.

blocks.title: Regression gate for a LangChain RAG slice

spans.text: Use this checklist before calling the build complete.

items.text: The retrieved evidence contains the facts stated in the answer.
Each citation points to a readable source title and location.
The negative test produces a qualified refusal or “not enough evidence.”
The trace shows retrieved IDs, scores or ranks, and final packed context.
The acceptance test reruns after source, model, framework, or chunking changes.

blocks.title: Release gate
blocks.prompt: What should block release even if the answer sounds helpful?

options.text: The trace includes too many useful details for developers.
A factual claim that is not supported by the retrieved cited evidence.
The app has only one model provider.

blocks.explanation: Groundedness is the top-level promise of a RAG app.
